svg.title: Flashing and Setup
svg.desc: Flashing and setup steps for MagicFocus; steps 1 to 3 are done once, steps 4 and 5 for each lens. Each step starts with a drawing of the device it is done on. 1, on the CoreS3, Gateway H2 and DIN Base stack, flash the H2 through the CoreS3: export the bridge binary from the Arduino IDE, upload Core2Programmer to the CoreS3, and write the H2 with esptool over USB; with a Core2, use the ESP32 Downloader instead. 2, on the same stack, flash MagicFocus onto the CoreS3 or Core2 with pio run -t upload; the H2 then restarts into the bridge firmware. 3, pair the motor, in three lanes, the Knob or Control Handle, the motor and the stack: 3a, on the Knob or handle, set Tilta CH1; 3b, on the motor, with its LED pink, double-click its button to pair; 3c, back on the Knob or handle, switch it off, marked as important: left on, its signals conflict with the H2's; 3d, on the stack, check that the MagicFocus tab shows Motor OK. 4, set up the camera and lens, in two lanes, the camera and lens above the motor: 4a, set the lens to MF with its AF/MF switch; 4b, on focus-by-wire lenses only, set the camera's focus ring to linked to rotation degree and disable its auto power-off; 4c, on the motor, hold its button for 3 seconds to calibrate it to the lens, and on a lens without end stops, stop the motor at both ends yourself. 5, on the stack, calibrate each lens: pick it with the arrows or a lenses.txt list, then on the Calib. tab aim the lidar, focus and save at least two points, and test the calibration with AF on, on the MagicFocus tab.
svg.text: Steps 1 to 3 once, steps 4 and 5 for each lens.
Flash the H2 through the CoreS3
Flash MagicFocus onto the CoreS3 or Core2
Set up the camera and lens
no end stops? manually stop motor at ends
